justification: Both are low-relief carvings showing a creature in profile with clawed extremities, but A depicts a densely detailed anthropomorphic winged figure with elaborately patterned garment, staff and bucket surrounded by dense rosette-and-vine filler, while B shows a single sparse, highly schematic quadruped/predator on an otherwise empty field with a plain arcing line beneath. The correspondence goes no further than 'an animal shown in profile in relief', which any tradition could produce independently; the compositional density, subject and rendering conventions differ entirely.
